title: POC Weekly Sync — Traffic Spike, 502s, and Rate-Limit Playbook
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on a mid-week traffic surge that caused transient 502s and aggressive rate-limit throttles. Team reviewed retry/backoff behavior, token-bucket settings, and temporary mitigation (graceful degradation + secondary model). Agreed next steps: log digs, tweak client backoff, enable per-customer token bucket, run staged load test next Wednesday.

Maya to send revised pilot pricing and per-minute cost calc by 2025-10-09

Enable temporary fallback model and add rate-limit header to responses, testing by 2025-10-11

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-10-07
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Dev Patel, Lena Ortiz (Redwood); Anika Rao, Ben Torres, Priya Singh, Samir Malhotra (Caravel)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be noisy): mid-week spike, transient 502s, rate-limit hits, client retries piled up, need for token-bucket per-customer and graceful fallback.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, I think we have a full room. Quick check — we on video?
[00:08] Anika Rao: Yeah, on video. Thanks Maya. Sorry for the scramble this week — the spike yesterday was messy.
[00:14] Dev Patel: No worries, Anika. We got your logs but there's a few signals we wanted to walk through. We saw a pattern of 502 bursts correlated with very high concurrent streams hitting the same model variant.
[00:27] Ben Torres: Right, from our side the ingress proxy showed a big fan-out at 13:42 UTC, a backlog, then a bunch of downstream timeouts. Some of our clients retried aggressively — maybe too aggressively.
[00:41] Priya Singh: We also noticed a latency tail increase before the 502s, like slow tokens building up in the KV cache region. Not sure if cache thrash is a real word, but something like that.
[00:55] Maya Chen: Got it. Two threads here: client-side retry/backoff and server-side capacity. Dev, can you pull up the telemetry we shared?
[01:03] Dev Patel: Sure, give me a sec. I'm sharing the dashboard — bear with the auto zoom. So this spike: you can see request rate jumps from baseline ~120 rps to 1.1k rps within a minute. CPU on the dedicated pool went up, and we start seeing 502s at 13:43.
[01:20] Samir Malhotra: The 502s in our logs look like gateway errors between our HTTP proxy and the pods. Some show 504s as well. We also saw TLS renegotiation oddities.
[01:34] Lena Ortiz: That's consistent with connection churn. One common mis-signal is client retry storms when they don't respect Retry-After headers.
[01:43] Anika Rao: Are we certain the Retry-After header was being emitted? I thought Redwood said it would return rate-limit headers.
[01:49] Dev Patel: We do send X-RateLimit-Limit and Retry-After in most cases, but in a high concurrency edge-case the header generation path can be delayed by a microservice queuing. We noted that earlier in the pilot, and it's on our backlog to reduce that tail.
[02:03] Ben Torres: OK, so headers intermittently missing — that explains downstream callers continuing immediate retries.
[02:09] Maya Chen: For the POC right now we want three quick mitigations: 1) Harden client backoff, 2) Enforce token-bucket at edge (per-customer), 3) Short-term fallback to a smaller, cheaper model when latency crosses threshold. Thoughts?
[02:22] Priya Singh: Fallback is attractive, but we worry about quality variance. We need an explicit A/B check so product owners know when responses are degraded.
[02:30] Dev Patel: We can do structured responses with a "confidence" flag and attach a header that indicates "fallback=true" so your app can decide. The runtime supports on-the-fly model swaps in the routing layer.
[02:40] Samir Malhotra: Also want to point out our own client retry config — right now we have exponential backoff but with a very small cap and jitter off. That's probably making the pile-up worse.
[02:50] Anika Rao: We'll adjust that, Samir. But please also help us understand why the 502s happened at the infra-level.
[02:57] Dev Patel: From an infra perspective, two likely candidates: ephemeral pod restarts causing connections to drop, or upstream kernel-level socket queue saturation. We flagged some OOM-killer events earlier this week in one node.
[03:11] Ben Torres: That sounds new — we didn't change models. Could the runtime be allocating more KV cache memory under the new prompt shapes?
[03:18] Priya Singh: We introduced multi-turn sessions with longer context, so yes token usage per request increased significantly. That can increase KV cache pressure.
[03:26] Maya Chen: Makes sense. Dev, can you run a memory profile across the model variant and show where the larger sequences live?
[03:34] Dev Patel: Yep, I'll produce a heap/mem profile and share. Quick note: quantization reduces memory but we didn't flip quantization on this variant because of quality. Another lever though.
[03:45] Anika Rao: We're open to trying quantization if latency improves and quality drop is bounded. Priya, are you comfortable running a small eval set?
[03:52] Priya Singh: Yes, I can run our top-100 queries and measure delta.
[03:56] [05:00] (rough jump — the call has some gaps in the automated transcript, ambient noise)
[05:00] Maya Chen: Back to rate-limits — we recommend a per-customer token-bucket in front of the Redwood endpoint. That prevents one tenant from consuming whole pool. We can provide config examples.
[05:14] Ben Torres: That would be helpful. We have multi-tenant traffic and didn't want to throttle shared infra globally.
[05:21] Dev Patel: I'll also propose an adaptive token-bucket: start with conservative tokens, allow burst, then decay. We'll post the sample config to the shared Confluence.
[05:31] Samir Malhotra: Could you also add guidance for client retry windows? For example, base 200ms, multiplier 2, max 30s, jitter enabled.
[05:39] Maya Chen: Yes — standard good-practice. We'll include that.
[05:44] Anika Rao: Quick question on observability: during the spike our logs were overwhelming. Is there a recommended trace-sampling strategy for spikes so we still capture meaningful spans?
[05:54] Dev Patel: We typically do rate-limited tail sampling: increase trace sampling for requests above X latency, and otherwise keep default 1%. For spikes, we enable dynamic tail-sampling to get more of the high-latency traces.
[06:06] Priya Singh: That would help debugging.
[06:10] [08:15] Ben Torres: One of the weird things we saw were clusters of 502s that all had the same downstream pod IP — it hints at a hot pod or connection leak.
[08:23] Dev Patel: Yeah, that can be connection affinity or sticky sessions to a hot GPU. Our routing tries to spread, but with long-lived KV caches some sessions can stick. We can evict stale KV cache entries after N minutes to reduce stickiness.
[08:38] Samir Malhotra: Is there a way to gracefully drain sessions off a node before autoscale removes it? We saw hard drops when nodes cycled.
[08:46] Dev Patel: We support connection draining at the runtime level, but it needs to be wired into your orchestrator's drain hooks. We can provide a drain-script sample that waits for open streams to finish and migrates KV cache when possible.
[08:59] Anika Rao: Great. On the short-term, what would be the minimal change to reduce 502 frequency for the next 48 hours?
[09:07] Maya Chen: From Redwood side: enable fallback model routing, reduce max concurrency per model instance, and emit Retry-After reliably. From Caravel side: implement backoff with jitter and cap client concurrency. Together that should cut down the retry storm and stop the gateway overload.
[09:24] Priya Singh: For fallback we want to flag any fallback responses so analytics can filter them — we'll need a header and a metric.
[09:32] Dev Patel: We'll add X-Redwood-Fallback: true and increment a fallback_count metric per request.
[09:39] Ben Torres: Also, can we add a short-term per-customer quota so one noisy user won't take down the test pool?
[09:46] Maya Chen: Yes, per-customer token bucket as mentioned. Dev will post config.
[09:50] [12:00] (noise and people grabbing coffee, short pauses)
[12:12] Samir Malhotra: I want to ask about 5xx classification — some of our 502s were misclassified in our alerting and didn't trigger the right runbooks. Can Redwood attach a more descriptive error payload?
[12:24] Dev Patel: We can add structured error codes in the JSON body and map them to typed errors: e.g., RDW-502-KV-THROTTLE vs RDW-502-POOL-OVERFLOW. That should help your alert routing.
[12:38] Anika Rao: Perfect. We'll update our alert mapping.
[12:42] Maya Chen: Let's talk about test plan. We propose a staged spike test: 1) small pilot 200->1k rps on a canary model for 5 minutes, 2) verify headers and fallback, 3) run full pilot with guarded throttles. Redwood SE on-call during the test.
[12:58] Priya Singh: Sounds good. I want to be present for step 2 to validate fallback results.
[13:04] Dev Patel: We'll prepare a load script and a checklist. Also we'll instrument success/fallback/latency histograms so we have an apples-to-apples comparison.
[13:14] Ben Torres: Timeline? We prefer next Wednesday the 15th. That gives us time to tune retry windows.
[13:20] Maya Chen: We can do the 15th. I'll block time and confirm SE availability.
[13:25] Anika Rao: One more thing — we had an internal compliance question: are audit logs available for Private deployment, and how long are request logs retained by default?
[13:34] Lena Ortiz: For Private we support configurable retention; default for hosted is 30 days but can be extended. Audit logs are available with the enterprise package and ship with KMS-integrated encryption. We'll share the SOC2 doc.
[13:47] Priya Singh: Please include info on redaction policies for PII and how to configure KMS.
[13:53] Maya Chen: Noted — I'll attach the security pack.
[13:57] [20:00] (mid-call detour about pricing briefly)
[20:10] Maya Chen: Quick pricing note: for pilot we can offer a blended rate for this dedicated pool while you run the POC; I'll follow up with a short spreadsheet.
[20:20] Ben Torres: Appreciate that.
[20:24] Dev Patel: Back to technicals — I'll also look at kernel socket backlog tuning on the node pool and send a recommended sysctl set. That often reduces edge timeouts when bursts happen.
[20:35] Samir Malhotra: Good idea. We'll need to review with infra team.
[20:40] Maya Chen: Ok last bit — communications and wrap. We'll do the shared doc: runbook, sample token-bucket config, client-retry sample, fallback header spec, and a checklist for the 15th spike test. Dev to share logs slice and memory/heap profile. Maya to send pricing and security docs. Customer to confirm test participants and runbook edits.
[20:59] Anika Rao: Thanks everyone. This was helpful. Any objections to the plan?
[21:05] Priya Singh: None from me.
[21:07] Ben Torres: All good.
[21:09] Maya Chen: I'll follow up with calendar invite and the Confluence link. Thanks all — we'll reconvene after the spike test.
[21:16] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: some timestamps approximate; occasional speaker attribution may be off due to overlapping audio.
